Vehicle.title: Vehicle
Vehicle.description: Represents a vehicle in the fleet.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Vehicle entity.

plate.description: The license plate number of the vehicle.

category.description: The category of the vehicle (e.g., LOGISTICO, EMPILHADEIRAS).

currentKm.description: The current mileage of the vehicle in kilometers.

active.description: Indicates whether the vehicle is currently active in the fleet.

notes.description: Any additional notes or observations about the vehicle.

Service.title: Service
Service.description: Represents a type of maintenance service that can be performed on a vehicle.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Service entity.

name.description: The name of the service (e.g., OIL CHANGE).

defaultMonths.description: The default periodicity of the service in months.

defaultKm.description: The default periodicity of the service in kilometers.

defaultSupplier.description: The default supplier for this service.

VehicleService.title: VehicleService
VehicleService.description: Represents a specific instance of a service performed on a vehicle.

id.description: Unique identifier for the VehicleService entity.

lastDate.description: The date when the service was last performed.

lastKm.description: The mileage at which the service was last performed.

supplier.description: The supplier who performed the service.

responsible.description: Reference to User. (Relationship: User 1:N VehicleService). The user responsible for the service.

nextDate.description: The calculated date for the next scheduled service.

nextKm.description: The calculated mileage for the next scheduled service.

status.description: The status of the service (OK, ALERT, DUE).

notes.description: Any notes related to this service instance.

attachments.description: References to Attachment. (Relationship: Attachment 1:N VehicleService). URLs of attached files (e.g., invoices, images).

createdAt.description: Timestamp of when this service was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp of when this service was last updated.

User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.  This corresponds to the Firebase Auth UID.

role.description: The role of the user (e.g., Admin, Operator, Read-only).

email.description: The email address of the user.

phone.description: The phone number of the user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Setting entity.  Likely a single document with a known ID.

alertDays.description: The number of days before a service is due to trigger an alert.

alertKmDelta.description: The kilometer delta before a service is due to trigger an alert.

webhookWhatsApp.description: The webhook URL for sending WhatsApp notifications.

Attachment.title: Attachment
Attachment.description: Represents a file attached to a VehicleService record.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Attachment entity.

fileName.description: The original name of the attached file.

fileType.description: The MIME type of the attached file (e.g., application/pdf, image/jpeg).

fileUrl.description: The URL where the attached file is stored.

uploadDate.description: The date and time when the file was uploaded.

VehicleServiceEvent.title: VehicleServiceEvent
VehicleServiceEvent.description: Represents an event (history) of a specific VehicleService.

id.description: Unique identifier for the VehicleServiceEvent entity.

eventDate.description: The date and time when the event occurred.

eventData.description: A JSON string containing the event data.  For example, the old and new values of a field that was updated.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to prioritize authorization independence, clarity, and scalability. It leverages denormalization to avoid hierarchical authorization dependencies and structural segregation to ensure homogeneous security postures within collections.

*   **/users/{userId}**: Stores user profiles, using the Firebase Auth UID as the document ID, enabling path-based ownership for user-specific data.
*   **/vehicles/{vehicleId}**: Stores vehicle information. All users with read access can list the vehicles.
*   **/services/{serviceId}**: Stores predefined service types.  Only admins have write access.
*   **/vehicles/{vehicleId}/vehicleServices/{vehicleServiceId}**: Represents specific instances of services performed on vehicles. The `vehicleId` is denormalized into this collection. The `responsible` field tracks which user performed this service. This enforces clear ownership and avoids the need for complex `get()` calls in security rules.
*   **/vehicles/{vehicleId}/vehicleServices/{vehicleServiceId}/attachments/{attachmentId}**: Stores attachments related to vehicle services. Authorization is simplified because it is nested under vehicleServices.
*   **/vehicles/{vehicleId}/vehicleServices/{vehicleServiceId}/events/{vehicleServiceEventId}**: Stores the event history of the vehicle service.
*   **/settings/{settingsId}**: Stores application-wide settings, with a single document (e.g., `settingsId = 'config'`).
*   **/roles_admin/{userId}**:  Documents in this collection indicate admin privileges. The existence of a document determines admin status. This allows us to implement QAPs.

**Authorization Independence:**

*   The `vehicleServices` subcollection denormalizes the `vehicleId`, avoiding the need to fetch the vehicle to authorize operations on vehicle services.

**QAPs Support:**

*   The segregation of admin roles into the `roles_admin` collection and user data into `/users/{userId}` enables efficient and secure list operations based on role or user ID.
*   By nesting `vehicleServices` as a subcollection of `vehicles`, listing vehicle services is naturally scoped to a particular vehicle, preventing broad, unfiltered queries.
